parole.testo: Denominal. From Aramaic אַבְזָרָא (ʾaḇzārā), ultimately from Middle Iranian; compare modern Persian ابزار (abzâr).

Borrowed from Aramaic בָּזִיכָא (bāzīḵā, “censer”), itself from Middle Iranian *bāžak (“cup”), ultimately derived from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂g- (“to distribute, allot”). Cognate with Old Armenian բաժակ (bažak, “cup, glass, mug”).

Borrowed from Aramaic נַוְולָא (nawlā, “loom”), a Middle Iranian word continued in Persian نول (nôl, “the outer part of the mouth; a beak, bill; a spout; the neck of a bottle; tube, channel; anything on which one leans or is supported; a whirlpool, vortex”), ultimately from Old Tamil 𑀦𑀽𑀮𑁆 (nūl).
